note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Senate only; West Virginia has no 2026 governor race (Gov. Morrisey elected 2024).

WV-senate.statusNote: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito (R) seeks a third term against Morgantown attorney Rachel Fetty Anderson (D). Capito won the May 12 Republican primary with 66.5%; Fetty Anderson won the Democratic primary with 33.2% of a five-way field. Constitution Party nominee S. Marshall Wilson is also on the November ballot.

WV-house-1.statusNote: Rep. Carol Miller (R) seeks re-election against Vince George (D) and independent Isaiah Rucker. Miller won the May 12, 2026 Republican primary with 72.1% and George won the Democratic primary with 53.0%. Positions are not researched yet.

WV-house-2.statusNote: Rep. Riley Moore (R) seeks re-election against Ace Parsi (D) and independent Christopher Whitcomb. Moore was unopposed in the May 12, 2026 Republican primary and Parsi won the Democratic primary with 39.8%. Positions are not researched yet.

candidates.name: Shelley Moore Capito
candidates.now: U.S. Senator; chair, Senate Environment and Public Works Committee
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2015 and previously a seven-term U.S. House member; before politics she was a career counselor at West Virginia State University and education official. Now chairs the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee. Won the May 12, 2026 Republican primary with 66.5% over Tom Willis and three others.
priorities: Broadband and infrastructure for rural West Virginia

cost.label: Frames affordability through tax relief: families will 'see their take-home pay increase by thousands of dollars' and small businesses will 'grow and hire more people' (Senate office)

health.label: Mixed: opposes the ACA broadly, yet was one of three Republicans who blocked repeal without a replacement and supported preserving the ACA's Medicaid expansion in any repeal bill (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Voted Yea on S. 5, the Laken Riley Act requiring DHS detention of migrants charged with theft, passed 64-35 (Senate roll call vote 7, 2025)

taxes.label: Championed the One Big Beautiful Bill as 'the largest tax cut in history', 'permanently extending and expanding on the successful Tax Cuts and Jobs Act' (Senate office)

climate.label: Opposes greenhouse gas emission caps, voted to curtail federal fracking rules, 17% lifetime League of Conservation Voters score; backs coal, carbon capture and nuclear (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Once identified as pro-choice, reversed in 2022 saying states should decide; voted for the Partial-Birth Abortion Ban and supports 20-week restrictions but opposed six-week bans (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted against the Freedom to Vote Act, calling it 'a partisan power grab' that 'fundamentally federalizes our elections' (Senate office)

candidates.name: Rachel Fetty Anderson
candidates.background: Public interest attorney and former Morgantown city council member who has represented children and families in West Virginia since 2007; mother of four. Homeschooled, she earned her law degree from the University of Iowa. Won the May 12, 2026 Democratic primary with 33.2% of a five-way field.
priorities: Healthcare as a benefit taxpayers have already earned

health.label: 'American taxpayers pay enough taxes to receive the best healthcare in the world': invest in Medicare, Medicaid and Tricare for all Americans, medical necessity over profit (campaign issues)

taxes.label: Eliminate the 'Buy, Borrow, Die' loophole and increase 'the marginal tax rate of earners of over $500,000.00 per year' (campaign issues)

climate.label: Government should 'encourage investment in sustainable energy sources that minimally affect the environment', manage coal plants cleanly, restore environmental protections (campaign issues)

education.label: Prioritizes 'developmentally appropriate' public education 'consistent with current research', including age-appropriate reproductive health education (campaign issues)

repro.label: Supports 'autonomous decision making over their bodies' and the right 'to choose or refuse medical care, including birth control' (campaign issues)

candidates.name: Riley Moore
candidates.background: Riley Moore has represented West Virginia's 2nd District since 2023; previously West Virginia State Treasurer. Unopposed in the May 12, 2026 Republican primary.

climate.label: 'Fossil fuels power America's economy and provide high-quality jobs to West Virginians', opposing efforts to 'shut down the coal industry and throttle our burgeoning natural gas sector' (campaign site)

education.label: 'A zip code should not determine a child's future': defends 'the Hope Scholarship program' and the 'Jump Start Savings Program' (campaign site)

repro.label: 'I believe in life from the moment of conception to the moment of natural death' and claims a '100% pro-life voting record' (campaign site)

immigration.label: 'The only acceptable level of illegal immigration is zero' and pledges to 'finish the border wall' (campaign site); also voted Yea on the Laken Riley Act, Jan 22, 2025 (House Clerk roll call 23)

democracy.label: Voted Yea on H.R. 22, the SAVE Act, Apr 10, 2025 (House Clerk roll call 102)

candidates.name: Ahsan Parsi
candidates.background: Ace (Ahsan) Parsi, a political organizer, is the Democratic nominee against Rep. Riley Moore in West Virginia's 2nd District, winning the May 12, 2026 primary with 39.8%.

cost.label: Mixed: would 'cut tariffs driving up prices on coffee, beef, OJ, and other groceries' while also proposing to 'invest in small farms' (campaign platform)

health.label: Would 'fund rural hospitals' and 'pursue a single-payer public option' (campaign platform)

housing.label: Backs 'tax incentives and zoning reform to build more housing so West Virginians can afford to stay in West Virginia' (campaign platform)

climate.label: Would 'diversify supply through wind, solar, and other sources to drive down heating bills' (campaign platform)

education.label: Wants to 'increase Title I funds for at-risk rural schools' and 'redirect lost funds for vouchers back into public schools' (campaign platform)

safety.label: Would 'defund ICE and reinvest the funds in community policing models that build trust between officers and the communities they serve' (campaign platform)

repro.label: Would 'protect the right to make personal healthcare decisions' (campaign platform)

democracy.label: Backs 'automatic voter registration for all eligible citizens: participation should be the default, not the obstacle' (campaign platform)
